tagline: Hands-free reading. The screen scrolls by itself.
appsHint: Scrollino only scrolls inside the apps you pick. Leave it empty to scroll everywhere.
disclosureWhy: Scrollino uses the Android accessibility service to scroll for you. It is the only way an app can move the screen of another app, like your e-book or PDF reader.
disclosureDoes: What it does: simulates a slow upward swipe, at the speed you choose, only while scrolling is on.
disclosureDoesNot: What it does not do: it does not read, collect, store or share anything on your screen. Scrollino has no internet access.
disclosureRestricted: If the switch is greyed out, open App info, tap ⋮ and choose Allow restricted settings, then try again.
serviceOffNotice: The accessibility service is off, so Scrollino can’t scroll yet.
controlsHint: Open your book, pull down the notification shade and tap Start. Pause and change the speed from there too.
notificationsOffNotice: Notifications are off. Scrollino’s Start and Pause buttons live in the notification shade.
serviceStuckNotice: Android stopped Scrollino’s service. Turn Scrollino off and on again in Accessibility.
